original_title: A year after scrapping streaming show, Disney confirms Princess And The Frog animated special still coming
summary_en: Good news for fans of Princess Tiana! After shelving a planned animated series, Disney has officially confirmed a new standalone special is in the works for Disney+.

en.title: Disney Confirms New Princess And The Frog Special After Cancelling Series
en.summary: Good news for fans of Princess Tiana! After shelving a planned animated series, Disney has officially confirmed a new standalone special is in the works for Disney+.
en.body:
After a period of uncertainty and a public sigh from its star, Disney is finally bringing new animated adventures of **Princess Tiana** to fans. A year after the much-hyped **The Princess and the Frog** animated series was unceremoniously scrapped, Walt Disney Animation Studios Chief Creative Officer **Jared Bush** has confirmed that a special project centered on the beloved character is officially in production for Disney+.

This news comes as a welcome, albeit delayed, development for fans who were disappointed by the cancellation of the series. The original plan was for an animated musical series that would have expanded Tiana's story, but it drifted for years before being quietly dropped. This followed a broader strategic shift at Disney+, which has been pulling back from producing long-form animated originals unless they are tied to major franchises like **Marvel** or **Star Wars**. The re-theming of Splash Mountain to **Tiana's Bayou Adventure** kept the character in the public eye, but concrete new content seemed elusive until now.

## A New Bayou Adventure

The upcoming special aims to deliver a complete story, rather than an ongoing narrative arc, positioning it more akin to a traditional television special or a featurette. **Jared Bush** confirmed that the project will include new songs and, crucially, will feature the original cast members reprising their iconic roles. This commitment to the original voice talent, particularly **Anika Noni Rose**, who publicly expressed her disappointment last year, is a significant win for the project and its fanbase. While details about the plot remain under wraps, the confirmation of new music and the return of the original cast suggests a genuine effort to capture the magic of the 2009 film.

> "It'll be a complete story, rather than an ongoing television series, with Bush describing it as something closer to a television special." — Collider

## What This Means for Fans

The decision to move forward with a special, rather than an open-ended series, indicates a more focused approach from Disney Animation. For viewers who loved **The Princess and the Frog**, this offers a concrete promise of more Tiana content, delivered in a format that allows for a self-contained narrative. It’s a clear signal that even as Disney recalibrates its streaming strategy, characters like Tiana still hold significant appeal. The stakes for this special are high: it needs to satisfy a dedicated fanbase while also proving the viability of standalone animated projects for the platform. Its success could pave the way for similar projects based on other beloved Disney properties that might not fit the mold of a full series.

## What's Next

While a release date has not yet been announced, the confirmation that the special is in actual production suggests it could arrive on Disney+ within the next year. Fans will be eagerly awaiting further details on the story and the new musical numbers.

content_raw: Disney has spent the last few years seeming not to know what it’s supposed to be doing with the cast of its 2009 animated hit  The Princess And The Frog . Sure, the entertainment giant was happy to re-theme the former Splash Mountain with Tiana and her bayou buddies a few years back, neatly replacing the ride’s previous Song Of The South  branding with a depiction of Black American characters a bit less likely to get it into public tussles with the NAACP. And Tiana remains in circulation in the company’s general princess branding, kept top-of-mind by a charismatic performance from Anika Noni Rose. But Rose herself expressed very public unhappiness last year , when Disney confirmed it was scrapping plans for an animated series centered on the character that had, after being announced to much fanfare back in 2020, spent years drifting around Disney+’s streaming schedule. All of which is to note a recent piece from  Collider , which confirms that, finally, at least  some  new  Princess And The Frog  content is in the works, even as Disney execs sound a little weird when trying to describe it. With the company having previously said that it’s pretty much abandoning making long-form animated content for Disney+ (part of an overall move away from streaming original content that’s seen the service dith out on basically any originals that aren’t Marvel, Star Wars, or Percy Jackson ), Walt Disney Animation Studios CCO Jared Bush has now confirmed that a Tiana  special of some kind, complete with the film’s original  cast on board to star in it, is  in actual production. His descriptions of the series—presumably the one that Disney originally floated back when it let everybody know it was killing  Tiana  the series, and featuring work from that series’ would-be showrunner, Joyce Sherri—does remain strangely vague, though: “I’m hesitant to give you the specifics,” Bush said. “I’d say it probably will feel more like a special to people. So, it’s not shorts. It’s a full story with a lot of songs as part of it. We have not announced a specific timing of that yet.” But he did assure fans: “That’s actually in active production. That will be out to people soon. New songs. Original cast. It is pretty spectacular.” All of this is, of course, separate from the rather odd comments Rose’s buddy Colman Domingo made back in July , when he started making noises about writing some sort of live-action project as a spin-off to the original movie. ( Princess And The Frog  remains, meanwhile, one of the only animated Disney films that the company’s live-action remake machine hasn’t come for yet.)
